concepts.def: Random (e.g. dice), systematic (every nth), stratified (proportional by group); each suits different investigations.
Numerical measurements: pebble size, river velocity, pedestrian counts; can be statistically analysed.
Descriptive non-numerical: photographs, sketches, interviews; capture meaning and perception.
Rating scale (e.g. minus 5 to plus 5) of qualities like cleanliness; used for environmental quality.
Statistical test of correlation between two ranked variables; values from minus 1 to plus 1.
Map using graded colours to show variation by area; e.g. population density or income across regions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Geographical Applications (Issue Evaluation & Fieldwork) — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Geographical Applications (Issue Evaluation & Fieldwork) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Geographical Applications (Issue Evaluation & Fieldwork).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
